question.text: Kaveri Opportunities Fund, a Category II AIF with total corpus INR 800 crore and estimated lifetime administrative/management expenses of INR 40 crore, is evaluating a buyout in Apex Realty Ltd. What is the maximum amount it may deploy in this single investee company under the standard Cat II concentration rule?

answer.text: INR 190 crore (25% of investable funds, i.e. corpus net of fund expenses)
INR 400 crore (50% limit applicable to all Cat II AIFs)

explanation.text: The Logic: A Cat I/II AIF's single-investee investment is capped at 25% of INVESTABLE FUNDS, not 25% of corpus. Investable funds = Corpus minus estimated administration and management expenses for the tenure of the fund. Here: Investable funds = 800 - 40 = INR 760 crore; 25% of 760 = INR 190 crore. The Trap: Option A applies 25% to the gross corpus and ignores the 'investable funds' definition. Option C uses a 50% figure that is not the standard Cat I/II single-investee cap. Option D applies the wrong percentage entirely. Note: The workbook defines investable funds as corpus net of estimated administration and management expenses for the life of the fund, and applies the 25% single-investee cap to that base for Category I and II AIFs.
